meta.name: DMG / EasiSystem™ Design DNA
meta.description: Design system, style, and visual-effects profile extracted directly from the live DMG/EasiSystem Next.js codebase (not an external reference) -- documents what is actually built, as of the claude/easisystem-homepage-redesign-vhwnfi branch.

primary.role: DMG Teal -- master brand color, primary CTAs, links, headline accents (teal-700)

secondary.role: ink-900 -- strongest text color, also the fill for the hero's animated pulse element

accent.role: sage-600 -- distinct category-badge accent (e.g. 'Guides'), kept separate from both brand teal and the saturated size/status colors

neutral.scale: Two independent neutral families: ink-900..ink-100 (cool green-tinted grays, text) and paper-0..paper-400/paper-cream (warm greige, surfaces)
neutral.usage: Ink scale used exclusively for text at every weight (headings ink-900 down to captions ink-300); paper scale used exclusively for backgrounds, borders and fills. Never crossed.

color.contrast_strategy: dark-on-light dominant -- high-contrast ink-900 text on paper-50/white surfaces, paired with soft/subtle borders and shadows rather than heavy dividers or dark surfaces

typography.font_style_notes: Single variable typeface (Manrope, weights 200-800) for both display and body -- a geometric, low-contrast grotesque described in the token source itself as 'clinical, precise, modern'. ss01/cv11 OpenType features enabled site-wide.

spacing.section_rhythm: Large gaps between major sections (80-96px), moderate padding within cards (20-24px) -- generous whitespace is explicitly called out as load-bearing in the token source's own comment ('Clinical layouts: generous whitespace')

layout.grid_system: CSS Grid, auto-fill minmax(280px, 1fr) on mobile/tablet collapsing to a fixed 3-column grid at the 1024px desktop breakpoint
layout.breakpoints: 1024px is the dominant desktop threshold used throughout; 640px used as a secondary mobile-specific cutoff in at least one card component
layout.alignment_tendency: strict grid for card layouts; left-aligned text blocks generally

shape.border_usage: subtle 1px hairline by default; a 2px 'thick' token exists but is rarely reached for
shape.divider_style: thin hairline borders in warm neutral tones (paper-300/400), no heavy rules

levels.high: 12-48px blur, 12-16% opacity (shadow-lg/xl), plus a teal-tinted shadow-brand variant for CTA emphasis

elevation.depth_cues: shadows (always green-black tinted, never pure black) + a small translateY lift on hover -- no blur/glass depth cues

iconography.style: custom brand-drawn outline/line-art illustrations, not a generic icon library
iconography.stroke_weight: thin, deliberately tuned per use case (several passes this session thinned/eroded stroke weight for small render sizes)
iconography.size_scale: contextual -- 44-58% of card width for corner-bleed watermark illustrations, fixed heights for hero diagram node icons
iconography.preferred_set: proprietary EasiSystem product/workflow line art (recolored to brand teal via CSS mask), not Feather/Lucide/etc.

motion.easing: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 1) for entrances/interactions, cubic-bezier(0.5, 0, 0.2, 1) for symmetric transitions -- explicitly 'no bounce' per the token source
motion.entrance_pattern: fade + slight translateY/scale-in (e.g. modal: translateY(12px) scale(0.98) to identity); card hover lift of -6px
motion.exit_pattern: reverse of entrance (fade out); reduced-motion collapses everything to instant
motion.philosophy: clinical and restrained -- motion is always tied to a specific meaning (hover = interactive, an ambient pulse = 'the system is alive', a headline stutter = literalizes the word 'Move') rather than decorative flourish. A handful of bespoke hero animations deliberately run far longer than the base 120-320ms scale (a 7s ambient pulse, a 1.47s entrance stutter) as intentional exceptions for ambient/one-shot moments, not the interaction norm. Every custom animation is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.

components.button_style: solid-fill primary (brand teal, shadow-brand, -1px hover lift), outlined secondary (teal border/text), borderless ghost -- all radius-sm (8px), semibold label, no bounce easing
components.input_style: not deeply exercised in this session's work; implied to follow the same radius-sm/hairline-border pattern as buttons
components.card_style: flat white or teal-tint surface, 1px hairline border, radius-md (12px), often a 4px top-edge accent bar (solid or gradient); isolate stacking context + overflow:hidden used consistently to contain corner-bleed decorative elements
components.navigation_pattern: sticky header (72px mobile / 100px desktop height), horizontal link row on desktop, hamburger + drawer on mobile
components.modal_style: centered overlay dialog, dark teal-tinted scrim, fade + scale-up entrance (12px/0.98 to identity), pill-shaped close button top-right
components.list_style: browser default list styling reset site-wide (no bullets/padding); custom badge/number markers used instead
components.component_notes: A recurring two-zone card pattern across ProductCard and WorkflowCard: a plain header zone (title/summary) plus a visually distinct tinted footer panel (CTA text + a low-opacity corner-bleed illustration), rather than one flat stack of content.

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: medical/clinical precision -- a single deep teal historically associated with surgical/healthcare branding, a geometric hexagon motif echoing the product logomark, no organic or soft shapes
aesthetic.era_influence: contemporary corporate SaaS / health-tech, no retro or ornamental influence

visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: text-led, with one supporting illustration per card/section rather than one dominant hero image
visual_language.focal_strategy: single hero element on the homepage (the ecosystem diagram); distributed interest / progressive reveal on listing pages via card grids
visual_language.contrast_level: high text contrast (near-black on off-white), low-contrast decorative elements (0.45-0.55 opacity illustrations)
visual_language.texture_usage: near-none -- a single very subtle full-page noise/grain overlay at 3.5% opacity, nothing else

composition.hierarchy_method: scale contrast + color weight (large display type and brand-teal accents pull focus, not spatial isolation)
composition.balance_type: asymmetric on the homepage hero (text left, diagram right); symmetric/grid-based on listing pages
composition.flow_direction: top-down, left-to-right; a loose Z-pattern on the hero (headline -> CTA -> visual)
composition.grouping_strategy: card-based grouping via a consistent two-zone header/footer pattern
composition.negative_space_role: active -- generous whitespace is treated as load-bearing to the calm/clinical feel, not incidental padding

imagery.photo_treatment: avoided in favor of line art almost everywhere; the one product page that used real photography was deliberately replaced with the same outline-illustration treatment as every other product, specifically for cross-page consistency
imagery.illustration_style: thin, brand-teal-recolored outline line art of the products/workflows in clinical use, shown as low-opacity corner-bleed watermarks
imagery.graphic_elements: hexagon motif (hero hub + node ring), thin gradient top-edge bars on cards
imagery.pattern_usage: one subtle full-page noise/grain texture overlay, nothing else
imagery.image_shape: rounded-rectangle crops (12-16px radius); no circular or angled crops except the hexagon hub/nodes themselves

interaction_feel.feedback_style: understated -- opacity/color shifts and small (1-6px) translateY lifts; no bounce/overshoot on ordinary interactive elements (overshoot easing is used exactly once, deliberately, for the hero's scroll-driven node assembly)
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: cards lift -6px with a brightening top accent bar and illustration opacity stepping 0.45 -> 0.55; buttons lift -1px with a deeper shadow
interaction_feel.transition_personality: smooth glide, snappy -- 120-320ms eased transitions, explicitly 'no bounce' per the design token source
interaction_feel.loading_style: not established in this session's work
interaction_feel.microinteraction_density: moderate overall, concentrated in the homepage hero (orbiting pulse, staggered node glow, headline stutter) and card hovers; restrained everywhere else

brand_voice_in_ui.formality: formal -- written for a healthcare-procurement audience
brand_voice_in_ui.cta_style: direct imperative paired with a small arrow ('Explore workflow →', 'Contact DMG')
brand_voice_in_ui.empty_state_approach: not established in this session's work
brand_voice_in_ui.error_tone: not established in this session's work (a --feedback-danger token exists but specific error copy wasn't authored)

overview.fallback_strategy: reduce to static -- every custom animation is explicitly gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, falling back to a fully-assembled, non-animating render
overview.primary_technology: CSS only (keyframes, transforms, offset-path), with Framer Motion's useScroll/useMotionValueEvent supplying the live scroll-progress values that drive those CSS custom properties. No Canvas, WebGL, or shader technology anywhere in the codebase.

background_effects.description: A fixed, full-viewport SVG feTurbulence noise texture at 3.5% opacity with an overlay blend mode -- a barely-perceptible static tactile grain, not an animated background

3d_elements.description: A CSS-only pseudo-3D hexagon 'ecosystem diagram' in the homepage hero: nodes fly in and settle on a tilted plane during scroll-driven assembly, then idle with a subtle continued sinusoidal tilt tied to scroll position. Not true WebGL/Three.js -- no real lighting or camera, just CSS 3D transforms plus per-node translateZ for a sense of depth.
3d_elements.technology: CSS 3D transforms (perspective, transform-style: preserve-3d, rotateX/rotateY, translateZ) -- no WebGL

params.lighting: none -- simulated via per-node opacity/scale depth cues instead of real shading
params.materials: flat brand-teal fills and CSS-mask-recolored line-art icons
params.geometry: a 6-point hexagon node ring plus a clip-path hexagon hub
params.interaction_model: hover/focus per node (click-through to that workflow); otherwise passive/scroll-driven

parallax.layers: 6 (each hero node sits at its own translateZ depth) plus the tilting stage itself
parallax.depth_range: small -- translateZ derived from each node's horizontal offset, plus a +-16px flight-in offset during assembly
parallax.speed_curve: eased overshoot (custom easeOutBack) during assembly; a linear/sinusoidal curve driven by continued scroll position once idle

scroll_triggered_animations.trigger_points: a single pinned hero section -- roughly the first 60-70% of a fixed scroll distance drives node fly-in/tilt-to-flat assembly, with the remainder as genuine 'idle' time before the section unpins
scroll_triggered_animations.animation_type: fade-up + scale-in + tilt, computed per node from one shared 0-1 scroll-progress value rather than a generic reveal library
scroll_triggered_animations.scrub_behavior: fully scrubbed and reversible -- driven directly by live scroll position, not a one-shot triggered animation; scrolling back up un-assembles it

text_effects.description: The hero headline's flexible word ('Move') hops sideways in three decaying bursts (two identical sharp ones, a third shorter and slower one) via CSS steps(1, jump-end) timing -- an instant per-keyframe snap rather than eased interpolation -- deliberately literalizing the word's own meaning. Plays once on mount only; not tied to scroll or hover.

params.animation_per_unit: single element, no internal stagger within the word
params.stagger: not applicable at the word level, though a comparable staggering technique is used elsewhere (the hero's per-node glow delays)
params.effect_style: mechanical stutter, glitch-adjacent but not a smooth glide

image_effects.description: Product/workflow illustrations brighten from 0.45 to 0.55 opacity on card hover, alongside a -6px card lift and a brightening top-edge gradient bar -- no distortion, tilt, or reveal-clip effects are used anywhere

params.hover_transform: translateY(-6px) card lift + opacity 0.45 -> 0.55 on the illustration
params.reveal_animation: none -- illustrations are always visible, just low-opacity

canvas_drawings.description: No <canvas> usage found anywhere in the codebase.

svg_animations.description: An SVG triangle continuously travels around a hand-built hexagonal CSS motion path once the hero is idle, blinking its own opacity on a separate loop -- synced so that each ring node's own glow animation peaks at the exact moment the triangle passes it (matched animation-duration plus a per-node animation-delay, exploiting the fact that a regular hexagon traversed at constant linear speed reaches each vertex at an exactly predictable time).

params.animation_method: CSS Motion Path (offset-path/offset-distance/offset-rotate: auto) plus separately-declared, precisely time-matched sibling keyframe animations -- not SMIL, not JS-driven position tracking
params.stroke_animation: none -- a filled triangle, not a drawn/animated stroke
params.filter_effects: a drop-shadow glow on the traveling triangle

visual_effects.composite_notes: The two most distinctive effects layer at the homepage hero: the CSS-3D-tilted node ring (3d_elements) plus the synced orbiting-pulse/node-glow system (svg_animations + scroll_effects), reading as one coherent 'living system' rather than two unrelated animations. Everything here is deliberately CSS + one JS scroll-tracking library -- performance_tier is 'lightweight' by design, and every effect gates behind prefers-reduced-motion. There is currently no Canvas, WebGL, particle, shader, or cursor-effect usage anywhere in the codebase; this profile's visual_effects dimension is entirely CSS-driven, worth stating explicitly since the schema's own field set leans toward assuming heavier rendering technology than this brand actually uses.
